summary: Boise NF lookout: a 1930 R-5 cab on a 10-foot base, with an R-6 cab set on that base in 1958; standing and drive-up, with staffing disputed.

staffing.status: disputed: firelookout.com and Daytrip Northwest say staffed every summer; Trails Off Road says unmanned

access.note: Dirt road from Highway 21 at Mores Creek Summit; no fees; 4WD in summer and early fall; snowshoe access in winter. Staffing is reported inconsistently in undated sources.

visit.trail_note: Dirt road from Mores Creek Summit, about 13 miles north of Idaho City; visitors can walk up to the concrete base and around the catwalk.

events.note: Region 5 cab on a 10-foot concrete base.
Lightning struck a tree 200 feet from the lookout; the lookout attendant put out the burning tree with a shovel. The item is dated January 28, 1945; the strike date is not given.
R-6 cab with catwalk built on the same 10-foot base.
Per a 1994 SITPA history, the association had stopped using a Sunset Mtn. lookout by 1940. The history gives no county, so the link to this tower is uncertain.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, October 16, 2011.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com and Daytrip Northwest say it is staffed every summer; Trails Off Road calls it unmanned. All three pages are undated, so the story reports the disagreement and does not pick a current status.
The NHLR 'Built 1958' field and the 1958 date on firelookout.com refer to the current R-6 cab. The original R-5 cab on the same base dates to 1930. Both are kept in events.

sources.title: A Brief History of the Southern Idaho Timber Protective Association 1904-1994

notes_for_editor: Staffing is disputed: firelookout.com and Daytrip Northwest say staffed every summer, Trails Off Road says unmanned, and none is dated. The brief's height_m 3.0 has no source among the pages read, so it is omitted. The 1994 SITPA history names a Sunset Mtn. lookout but gives no location; the story flags the uncertainty rather than linking it. No rental listing turned up; no Boise NF or recreation.gov page was read. The event dated 1940 is a SITPA-era event that may belong to another mountain.
